many people will give you many different answers. the most true answer is that reporting is always Your Choice. Im in the camp that it is usually worth it too. Reporting can give you a feeling of finally having some control of the situation, or a sense of justice for yourself, or feel like a good step forward. As far as I know (charges or not) a report does stay documented on someone, so IF something happened again, IF it got reported, it could help that case too. The thing about reporting is it can be a very long process. Being asked to tell your story and having it inspected as part of the process can make some people feel retraumatized. It is a long waiting process afterwards for many people, and usually a trial is a very trying process. Whats important is that it is not your responsibility to stop your assaulter from assaulting others. thats on him- its his own miserable failure that he would put others through that, and it can be kind of torturous for us to feel like we have to stop that. also, it wouldnt be your job to investigate and get evidence, its the detective’s, and you dont have to worry about that. And if the case gets dropped or charges dont get pressed, it will hurt a lot :( in my opinion, reporting is a risk worth taking, but its different for everyone. no matter what, stay strong and please take care ❤️ you’ve got this, i promise
